The matcher supports only two wildcards: `*` and `?`. `[abc]` is not a character class.

- `*` matches any run of characters, including none (src/filter.zig:64-67, 77-79). The test `"*.zig"` matches `foo.zig` (src/filter.zig:322).
- `?` matches exactly one character (src/filter.zig:61). The test shows `file?.log` matches `file1.log` but not `file10.log` (src/filter.zig:325-326).
- A trailing `/` is stripped from the pattern, so `target/` matches `target` (src/filter.zig:52-54, 324).
- Any other character, `[` included, is compared literally (src/filter.zig:61). So `[abc]` would only match a name containing the literal text `[abc]`.

The context does not show how `--exclude`/`--include` flags are parsed. It also doesn't show the README or GUIA docs, which would confirm the documented syntax. The patterns do reach `matchPattern` through `excluded_patterns` and `included_patterns` (src/filter.zig:286, 309).
